title: Initial setup
subtitle: A few steps and {appName} is ready to run.

language.title: Choose your language
language.description: The setup runs in this language. It is also the language of the mails and reports of your own organisation. You can change both later.

card.title: English
card.description: Set up in English, with mails and reports in English.

token.title: Confirm that you run this server
token.description: Only someone with access to the server can set up {appName}. The setup token proves it.
token.what: The setup token is a one-time code that proves you operate this server: only someone who can read the server's log can see it. It stops working once the setup is finished.
token.whereLog: The installer printed it at the end of the installation. To show it again, run this on the server (in the directory of your installation; /opt/restow is the default):
token.whereEnvironment: This server takes its setup token from the RESTOW_SETUP_TOKEN variable in its environment (.env). Enter that value.
token.restart: Each restart of the api issues a new token. Use the one printed last.
token.label: Setup token
token.hint: Upper or lower case and dashes do not matter.

error.invalid: This is not the setup token of this server. Copy it again from the log.
error.changed: The setup token has changed, probably because the api restarted. Enter the token it printed last. Your entries are kept.
error.failed: The token could not be checked. Try again.

disclaimer.title: Your responsibility as operator
disclaimer.description: Please read this notice. {appName} cannot be used until you accept it.
disclaimer.intro: {appName} is a tool for backup and archiving. It writes your data to storage that you operate and helps you get it back. It does not run that storage for you, and it cannot make your infrastructure safe. What happens on the hardware and storage layer is your responsibility as operator.

strategy.title: No replacement for a backup strategy
strategy.body: {appName} does not replace a backup strategy. Follow the 3-2-1 rule: three copies of your data, on two kinds of media, one of them off site or offline. Keep an independent copy that {appName} cannot reach or delete. Especially during the beta, {appName} must never be your only backup.

storage.title: Hardware and storage
storage.body: You are responsible for the servers, disks, networks and storage targets underneath, and for their redundancy, capacity and health. If a storage target fails, runs full, is lost or is not backed up separately, {appName} cannot repair that or bring the data back.

immutability.title: Ransomware and deletion
immutability.body: Data is only immutable if the storage makes it so. Without WORM or Object Lock configured on the storage target, anyone who can reach it, ransomware and a compromised account included, can change or delete your backups and archive. Protecting the storage against ransomware and deletion is your responsibility.

keys.title: Encryption keys
keys.body: Your data is encrypted with keys derived from the master key of this installation. You are responsible for keeping that key safe and stored apart from the data. If the master key is lost, the data cannot be decrypted by anyone and cannot be recovered.

security.title: Network and access
security.body: You are responsible for the security of the server, the network, the accounts and the credentials that reach {appName} and its storage: updates, firewall, HTTPS, strong sign-in, and who may access what.

restore.title: Test your restores
restore.body: Test restores regularly and check the results, in addition to the verification {appName} runs itself. A backup you have never restored is one you cannot rely on.

gobd.title: Archive and GoBD
gobd.body: The archive features are designed for GoBD-compliant use. Whether your whole procedure is compliant, including process documentation, retention periods, access rights, organizational measures and the storage behind the archive, is your responsibility. {appName} does not give legal or tax advice.

warranty.title: No warranty
warranty.body: {appName} is provided under its license terms and without warranty beyond them and beyond what mandatory law requires.

disclaimer.accept: I have read this notice and accept it. I understand that, as operator of this installation, I am responsible for the points above.
disclaimer.failed: Your acceptance could not be saved.
disclaimer.serverRequired: The notice has to be accepted before the setup can be saved.
disclaimer.versionChanged: The notice was updated. Reload the page to read the current version.

existing.title: Operator responsibility notice
existing.description: This installation was set up before this notice existed, or the notice was updated. Please read it and accept it to keep using {appName}.
existing.needAdministrator: An owner or administrator of the provider team has to accept this notice first. Ask one of them to sign in and accept it, or sign out.

mode.title: How do you run {appName}?
mode.description: You can change the mode later in the settings.
mode.localDescription: Reachable via IP address or localhost, without a public domain. Sign-in with the emergency password.
mode.publicDescription: Reachable via your own domain with HTTPS. Passkeys are available.

publicUrl.label: Public URL
publicUrl.hint: Exactly the address browsers open. It defines the passkey domain and the Entra redirect URI.

passkey.title: Passkey readiness
passkey.ready: Passkeys are offered on this installation.
passkey.notReady: Passkeys are not offered yet. Until then the emergency sign-in with password applies.

reasons.mode_not_public: Local mode does not bind a domain, which WebAuthn requires.
reasons.no_public_url: No valid public URL is set.
reasons.not_https: The public URL is not served over HTTPS.
reasons.origin_mismatch: The browser reports a different origin than the configured URL.

admin.title: Your organisation and the first admin account
admin.description: The organisation is the one that runs this installation. The admin account is the provider admin: it sets up {appName} and manages everything in it.

organisation.label: Name of your organisation
organisation.hint: The organisation that runs this installation, for example your company. {appName} sets it up as your own organisation, the place for your own backups.

password.label: Emergency password
password.hint: The password is the emergency path. Use a password manager. Right after signing in you set up an authenticator app; from then on {appName} asks for its code together with the password.

admin.passkeyHint: Once passkey readiness is reached, you can add a passkey under Sign-in security in the user menu.

mail.title: How does {appName} send notifications?
mail.description: Used for reports, alerts and invitations. The journal intake for the archive is separate from this.

skip.explanation: Mail is optional. Without it {appName} sends no alert or report e-mails, and invitations and set-password links are not sent by mail: you copy the link and pass it on yourself. You can set it up later under Installation → Notification mail.
skip.skipped: You skipped this step. Fill in the form and choose Next to set up mail now.

smtp.usernameHint: Leave empty if the server does not require authentication.
smtp.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown in plain text.

graph.hint: Uses the Microsoft app registration as an application. Requires the Mail.Send application permission with admin consent; see https://docs.restowbackup.com/administrators/setup-wizard/.

sendTest.label: Send a test message to the admin account
sendTest.hint: Shows right away whether the transport works. A failure does not block the setup.

review.title: Review
review.description: Check your entries and finish the setup.

result.testSendFailed: The test message could not be sent: {error}
result.signInFailed: The setup is saved, but the automatic sign-in did not work. Please sign in manually.
result.alreadyConfigured: This installation is already set up.
result.failed: The setup could not be saved.
result.administratorExists: An earlier, unfinished setup already created an administrator. Continue with that administrator's email and password.
result.configurationIncomplete: The server configuration is incomplete. Set {settings} in the server environment and restart {appName}, then finish the setup.
result.ownOrganisationFailed: The setup is saved, but your own organisation could not be created. Create it from the overview.
